sources.citation: Luke Initiative for Scripture Translation / The Seed Company. 2022 (source files dated 2025-07-10). Sanga Language Project: The Holy Bible in the Sanga language of Nigeria — Matthew and Luke [xsn]. USFM/HTML, CC BY-SA 4.0, distributed by eBible.org (id xsn, 'XSNLIZ').
sources.note: Primary text only, no front matter or orthography note. The practical orthography writes ǝ (3,134 tokens) but marks no tone: only 2 acute and 2 grave accents in the two books combined. This is orthographic practice, not a statement about the sound system.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-92. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210 (open access).
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.1 Phonology (pp. 54-58) describes only ɛBoze as the exemplar ('All East Kainji languages so far studied have a relatively simple phonology and broadly resemble one another'); tones: Boze has four level tones plus glides; 'Other East Kainji languages have much reduced systems.. Shimizu (1979, 1982a) usually transcribes the tonal systems in his lists as High and Low or High, Low and Downstep'. Sanga appears only in Table 1 (p. 49, status 'Vigorous', source column empty), the Fig. 5 tree (Lemoro-Sanga node) and Table 12 ('arm/hand' ò-ʔàra / tà-ʔàra). The word 'stress' occurs nowh…
